axes.brief:
Competitive presidential and legislative elections, popular recall and referendums, legislative scrutiny and constitutional adjudication anchor democratic authority.
Focused six-question reassessment: The Referendum Act provides citizen proposal routes and binding legislative principles subject to exclusions. A personally elected presidency is distinct from cabinet appointment; executive emergency orders require legislative confirmation, while presidential terms remain constrained.
axes.counterEvidence:
The 2025 Constitutional Court deadlock and contested December restoration show substantial institutional strain. Opposition control of the legislature is real; executive preferences and parliamentary outcomes must not be conflated. Emergency powers and party-dissolution procedures qualify absolute claims.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. The Referendum Act provides citizen proposal routes and binding legislative principles subject to exclusions. A personally elected presidency is distinct from cabinet appointment; executive emergency orders require legislative confirmation, while presidential terms remain constrained.
